name: OnePlan
tagline: Enterprise strategic portfolio management that sits on top of Microsoft 365, Project, Jira and Azure DevOps and rolls everything up into roadmaps, capacity plans and financials.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. Sold through quoted enterprise tiers rather than a public self-serve price.

verdictSummary: OnePlan is not a planning app, it is a aggregation layer: it pulls work from Project for the web, Planner, Azure DevOps, Jira and spreadsheets, then normalizes it into one portfolio with resource capacity, demand intake, financials and scenario modeling. An agent can absolutely build you a pretty local roadmap with a capacity heatmap, and that is a fun weekend. What it cannot build is the twenty live connectors, the entra ID tenant mapping, the approval workflows that finance and the PMO actually sign off on, or the agreement among six department heads that this is the single source of truth. Nobody buys this for themselves either, which makes the phrase personal replacement a bit of a category error. The consolation build below is a decent one-person portfolio planner and nothing more.
coreLoopDIY: A local portfolio board where you enter projects, assign people at percentage allocations across months, and see which months blow past capacity.
requirements: CSV exports from whatever tracker you use, re-imported by hand
Willingness to be the only user
whatYouLose: Live two-way sync with Project, Planner, Jira and Azure DevOps, which is most of the actual product
Entra ID / SSO, role-based permissions and audit trails that enterprise buyers require
Demand intake forms, scoring and approval gates that turn requests into funded projects
Financial modeling against actuals, cost types and multi-year budgets
Anyone else being able to see or trust your numbers
moatNotes: The Microsoft-ecosystem plumbing is the product. Rebuilding one connector properly is longer than rebuilding the whole UI.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the problem is organizational, not technical. A PMO buys OnePlan so that finance, delivery leads and executives are arguing over one table instead of eleven spreadsheets, and so the data arrives there automatically from tools teams already use. The UI is replaceable. The consensus, the connectors and the audit story are not, and no amount of local SQLite fixes the fact that your colleagues will not type their allocations into your laptop.
notes: A single-user portfolio planner is a weekend; a portfolio everyone agrees on is not. The moat is the Microsoft and Jira connector plumbing plus the governance workflow that makes the rollup authoritative.
prompt:
Build a local, single-user project portfolio planner called "Smallplan". No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, non negotiable:
- Next.js 15 with the App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind.
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/smallplan.db, schema created on first boot.
- Server Actions for all mutations. No separate API layer, no ORM.
- Runs with `npm run dev` on localhost only.

Data model:
- people: id, name, weeklyHours, costPerHour (nullable).
- projects: id, name, status (idea, approved, active, done), startMonth, endMonth, strategicGoal (free text), estimatedCost (nullable), priority int.
- allocations: id, projectId, personId, month (YYYY-MM), percent (0 to 100).

Screens:
1. Portfolio: table of projects sortable by priority and status, inline edit, create and delete.
2. Roadmap: horizontal month-by-month timeline bar per project across the next 18 months, grouped by strategicGoal, colored by status. Plain CSS grid, no charting library.
3. Capacity: heatmap of people down the rows, months across the columns, each cell showing total allocated percent. Green under 80, amber 80 to 100, red over 100. Clicking a cell opens an editor for that person-month's allocations.
4. Scenarios: a toggle list of projects; unchecked projects are excluded from the capacity math so you can test what happens if something is cut. Scenario state is local component state, not persisted.

Also:
- CSV import and export for projects, people and allocations. Import is upsert by name.
- A single summary bar: active project count, total estimated cost, count of over-allocated person-months.
- Seed script with 8 projects and 5 people so the UI is not empty on first run.

Explicitly out of scope: authentication, multi-user, Jira or Microsoft integrations, notifications, approval workflows, financial actuals, mobile layout. Do not add them.

Any secrets go in .env.example. Write a README with setup, the data model, and a short section titled "what this is not" that says this is not a PPM system of record.
